title: scale-down cache window causes transient tenant-affinity rebind for Dedicated API keys
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent 403s and cross-tenant access errors after autoscaling events. Root cause is a race between node scale-down eviction and the API-key tenant-affinity cache eviction window. During graceful drain, a short period where the key-to-tenant mapping is removed from local cache but not yet rehydrated to the global store allowed requests to be routed to a different tenant affinity fast-path, producing authorization failures or temporary access to stale tenant context. Impact: observed across Hosted-Dedicated hybrid routes and Private VPCs with sticky affinity enabled; customers saw ~2-10 requests/min failing for 15-45 minutes during peak scale events. Several enterprise customers escalated for potential data exposure risk (investigation shows no persisted cross-tenant writes, only transient misbound request context).
root_cause: A node scale-down flow triggers local cache invalidation of apikey->tenant mappings before the global reconciliation loop completes. Eviction removes the mapping from the local fast-path and a subsequent request during reconnection can be routed to a different warm node which has a stale affinity placeholder; the routing layer uses the placeholder and a VM-local auth short-circuit, resulting in transient tenant context misbind.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a Dedicated pool with sticky tenant-affinity and small scale-down grace (30s).
2) Rapidly scale down nodes while sending concurrent requests signed with the same API key across the pool.
3) Observe intermittent 403s and requests with incorrect tenant headers in the access logs on the receiving nodes.
Notes: repro requires fast node churn and short reconcilation window; lab harness attached in links.
mitigation: Short-term: increased the local cache grace window from 30s to 5m and disabled the local fast-path short-circuit for dedicated pools via runtime flag on 2026-03-06 to stop further customer impact. Also opened controlled communication to affected customers. Long-term fix: ensure atomic handoff of apikey->tenant bindings during node eviction (handshake + sticky lease renewal) and add invariant checks in router to reject ambiguous affinity entries.
fix_summary: Implemented a two-phase eviction: (1) mark mapping as 'draining' and continue honoring local mapping until global handshake completes, (2) perform atomic swap only after receiving acknowledgement from routing layer. Added additional integration tests and a canary rollout plan. Patch: runtime PR #7894.
qa_plan: Integration test harness simulating rapid scale-up/down with multi-tenant traffic
Canary: 1% of dedicated traffic for 72 hours with strict observability thresholds
Run replay of affected customer request traces in staging and verify no tenant mismatch
comments: 2026-03-05 - Ava Chen: Initial pager impact reported by two enterprise dedicated customers, notified on-call and created ENG-50789. Immediate mitigation suggested: raise cache TTL and disable local short-circuit.

2026-03-06 - Ravi Patel: Applied runtime flag to increase cache grace window to 5m and disabled fast-path in production; customer errors dropped to background noise. Communicated interim fix to SEs and affected customers.
2026-03-07 - Nate Brooks (SRE): Observed no regression in latency after runtime flag change. Added metric for 'ambiguous-affinity-events' to Grafana.
2026-03-09 - Priya Nair (Security): Performed preliminary review of logs; no evidence of persisted cross-tenant writes. Recommend full postmortem and external customer write-up once fix is validated.

2026-03-11 - Ravi Patel: Submitted PR #7894 implementing two-phase eviction and handshake. Added detailed integration tests in runtime/test/affinity. Requesting review from kern/route owners. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7894
2026-03-12 - Marcos (Routing): Reviewed PR and requested tighter invariants around lease expiry; updated algorithm to include sequence checks. Responded in PR review thread.
